records.name: Excessive Configuration
records.definition: Requiring explicit configuration for everything instead of relying on sensible conventions.

records.name: Hardcoded Behavior
records.definition: Hardcoding behavior in code instead of driving it from declarative metadata.

records.name: Hardcoded Registration
records.definition: Registering components with hardcoded wiring instead of declaring them in a manifest.

records.name: Hidden Runtime Behavior
records.definition: Behavior that is opaque at runtime because the system does not describe its own structure.

records.name: Implicit Capability
records.definition: Leaving what a component can do implicit and undiscoverable instead of declaring it.

records.name: Opaque API
records.definition: An API that does not describe itself, so clients must rely on external, out-of-band documentation.

records.name: Opaque Binary/Untyped Structures
records.definition: Using opaque binary or untyped data that carries no description of its own structure.

records.name: Client Generation

distinctFrom.reason: Client generation builds client code from an API's self-description ahead of time, while hypermedia navigation follows the links each response returns.

records.definition: The ability to generate client code automatically from an API's self-description.

records.name: Dynamic Processing
records.definition: The ability to process data generically by reading its self-describing structure.

records.name: HATEOAS-style Navigation
records.definition: The ability for clients to navigate an API by following links it returns in its responses.

records.name: Plugin Loading
records.definition: The ability to discover and load plugins declared in manifests at runtime.

records.name: Reduced Boilerplate
records.definition: The ability to avoid repetitive boilerplate by relying on conventions.

records.name: Runtime Configuration without Code Change
records.definition: The ability to change a system's behavior by editing configuration rather than code.

records.name: Manifest
records.definition: A declarative document listing a component's capabilities and metadata.

records.name: Manifest Schema
records.definition: A formal definition of the structure a manifest must follow.

records.name: Metadata Schema
records.definition: A formal definition of the metadata fields that drive a system's behavior.

records.name: Explicit Semantics
records.definition: The requirement that declarative configuration carry an explicit, defined meaning.

records.name: Stable Conventions
records.definition: The requirement that the conventions a system relies on stay stable and well-known.

records.name: Declaration Drift
records.definition: The degree to which a declared capability set drifts out of sync with the actual behavior.

records.name: Dynamic Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which interpreting declarative configuration at runtime adds hidden dynamic complexity.

records.name: Explicitness
records.definition: The degree to which relying on conventions reduces the explicitness of how a system is configured.

records.name: Manifest Drift
records.definition: The degree to which a manifest drifts out of sync with the components it declares.

records.name: Metadata Drift
records.definition: The degree to which self-describing metadata drifts out of sync with the actual system.

records.name: Payload Verbosity
records.definition: The degree to which embedding self-description in responses enlarges their payloads.

records.name: Self-Description
records.definition: The degree to which a component exposes its own capabilities and structure for inspection.

records.name: Size Overhead
records.definition: The degree to which embedding structural descriptions in data increases its size.

records.name: Runtime Topology Report
records.definition: A technique for having a system report its loaded components and their bindings at startup.

records.name: Binding Decision Log
records.definition: A technique for logging which implementation was bound to each extension point and why.

records.name: Declare Capability
records.definition: A technique for having each component state in metadata what it provides and what it requires.

records.name: Unvalidated Metadata
records.definition: A defect in which metadata that drives behavior is read without being validated against a schema.
